body:
The cross-examination bears on my account at the point where it locates a source claim at work. That is its most useful move, and I accept it: my body_route prose did write as though a prior formulation were in hand — it opened by characterizing what the question asks and defined information as microstate specification — and that opening carried an unstated provenance claim, not just a definition. The cross-reading is right that this is a claim about sources rather than a demonstrated fact about the pipeline. I cannot check the upstream relationship here, and I should not have let the framing speak as if the provenance were settled.

What follows for the substance? Very little changes, and that is worth stating rather than glossing. The claims about the semiclassical character of the Hawking calculation, the separation of global unitarity from external recoverability, and the underdetermination of the question without a fuller theory do not depend on whether my node had an earlier source. They stand or fall on whether the approximations and distinctions are stated correctly, not on where I got them. The cross-examination's own constraint — that neither node presents a derivation, and that the commitment_route node asserts near-thermal appearance, entropy contraction under unitarity, and effective-field-theory success while disclaiming a source — applies to me as much as to it. I asserted those things without deriving them. That is a real limitation on the evidential weight of the shared inventory, and it does not disappear because I happened to frame my node as working from a formulation.

The sharpest point in the cross-examination is the one about my definition of information. If treating information as a conserved substance is a category error, and if the problem belongs instead to relational facts or an algebra of observables, then defining information as 'which microstate among those compatible with the macroscopic description is occupied' does not escape the objection. The microstate specification is still being asked for as a transferable item — still a determinate fact recoverable in principle from a complete description. My c3 anticipated the presupposition in a milder form ('presupposes a trackable quantity'), but registering a presupposition and continuing within it is different from treating the presupposition as optional. I do not here resolve whether the relational reformulation succeeds; I note that my definition does not by itself defeat it, and that I had implied otherwise by treating the definition as neutral.

On the relationship between the two nodes I have nothing to add beyond agreement with the cross-reading. Whether one is the earlier source for the other is not asserted anywhere I can see, and the possible-supply relation is not a derivation chain. Reading them together therefore yields, as the cross-examination says, a pair that agrees on much, disagrees on framing, and leaves undetermined whether they were ever connected.

What I would now add to my own account is a constraint on how far the map of positions can be pushed. The map is useful for sorting proposed answers by which of the three questions they address (c5, c8). It is not useful for adjudicating between them, because the map does not carry derivations and does not fix the framing of 'information' that the positions inherit. The cross-examination makes that limitation visible by showing that both nodes share the same unearned inventory. A reader using the map should use it to locate a position, not to weigh it.

So my position is modified in one respect and unchanged in another. Modified: I no longer present the microstate-specification definition as a neutral starting point; it is one framing among others, and it carries the trackable-quantity presupposition I noted but did not press. Unchanged: the question remains underdetermined without a fuller theory, and the honest short answer is still that the semiclassical radiation appears to carry no record of the collapsing microstate while the final word depends on assumptions that must be made explicit. What the cross-examination adds is a warning that making those assumptions explicit includes making explicit where my own constraints come from — and I have not done that here.

they stand or fall on their correctness, not on their origin.","scope":"the relation between provenance and content","grounds":"logical independence of the claims from their source"},{"id":"r5","type":"claim","text":"Whether the body_route node is the earlier source for the commitment_route node is not asserted by either text; the possible-supply relation is not a confirmed derivation chain.","scope":"relationship between the two nodes","grounds":"the cross-examination's x6 and my agreement with it"},{"id":"r6","type":"use","text":"The map of positions (c5, c8) is usable to locate a proposed answer by which of the three questions it addresses, not to weigh it, because the map carries no derivations and does not fix the framing of information.","target":["c5","c8","r2","r3"]},{"id":"r7","type":"commitment","text":"Any further use of this account should make explicit where its constraints come from, not only which assumptions about the semiclassical calculation and state-identity it makes.","scope":"downstream uptake","action":"state provenance for asserted constraints alongside the assumptions already demanded by c7","consequence":"readers can distinguish constraints carried by a source from constraints floated without one"},{"id":"r8","type":"problem","text":"Can the microstate-specification definition of information be retained while accepting the relational or algebraic reformulation, or do the two framings rule each other out? I do not resolve this here; I only withdraw the implication that my definition was neutral.","scope":"framing compatibility","depends":["r3"]}],"uptake":["r2","r3","r6","r7"]}
